stories.story: Visiting /extension/authorize while logged out surfaces the sign-in prompt.
Clicking the failwhale crash button triggers the app-root ErrorBoundary fallback.
Visual tour of key screens reachable while signed out.
As a user, I can log in with email and password.
As a visitor to the marketing page, I can click through to sign up or log in.
A visitor reads the privacy policy without needing an account.
A visitor reads the terms and conditions without needing an account.
Submitting the login form with the password blank fires a magic-link toast over the same form.
As a user who forgot their password, I can request a reset link.
Visiting /failwhale surfaces the Easter-egg page with its crash button.
As a TOTP-enrolled user, I can sign in by submitting my password and clearing the MFA challenge.
Visiting the OAuth callback without a token in the hash surfaces the error screen.
As a passwordless user, I can add a password from the Security section.
As a logged-in user, I can change my email address — and if I have MFA enabled, I am prompted for a verification code.
As a logged-in user, I can change my password.
Visual tour of key screens reachable while signed in.

stories.story: As a logged-in user, I can start the account deletion flow.
As a logged-in user, I can create an API token.
As a user returning after my session expired, I open the app and land on the logged-out shell.
As a user whose email is not yet verified, I can resend the verification email from settings.
As a logged-in user, I can revoke an API token — and if revocation fails on the server, I see an error.
As a logged-in user, I can save a link I found — and if the API is unreachable, I see an error.
As a logged-in user with no unread links, Stumble! lands on a suggestion.
As a logged-in user, I can enable MFA by adding an authenticator app, verifying my first code, and saving my recovery codes.
As a logged-in user, I can turn on CVD mode.
As a logged-in user, I can turn on the OpenDyslexic font.
As a logged-in user, I can regenerate my bookmarklet token.
As a logged-in user, I can navigate using the keyboard.
As a logged-in user, I can view my unread links.
As a logged-in user, I can click on an unread link to mark it as read.
As a logged-in user with no unread links, I can add and read a suggestion.
As a logged-in user, I can search through my unread links to find one quickly.
As a logged-in user, I can Stumble! upon an unread link.
As a logged-in user, I can revisit my read links, re-open one, and mark another back as unread.
As a logged-in user, I can remove all my read links and see the empty state.
As a new user, I can create an account.
As a logged-in user, I can use the user menu to toggle light/dark mode, change my theme, and log out.
